FY 2025-26 reinforced the Company’s evolution into a 
gaming-first global platform. With gaming contributing nearly 
90% of EBITDA, Nazara entered a new phase of growth 
supported by enduring intellectual property, operating 
excellence and scalable capabilities.
The establishment of Centres of Excellence across User 
Acquisition, Data Analytics, Artificial Intelligence, Growth 
and Product further strengthened the operating framework 
across the portfolio. These shared capabilities enable greater 
efficiency, stronger execution and improved collaboration 
across businesses. AI also became increasingly embedded 
across the game lifecycle, supporting innovation, accelerating 
development cycles and enhancing player engagement. 
As these capabilities evolve, they are strengthening Nazara’s 
ability to develop, operate and scale gaming experiences 
more effectively. The proposed strategic acquisition of 
Bluetile and BestPlay will bring global scale, AI-native 
development expertise and a powerful engagement 
ecosystem, further strengthening the Company’s growth 
engine.
The impact of these strategic developments was reflected 
in record revenues, the highest EBITDA in Nazara’s history 
and strong cash generation, demonstrating the Company’s 
ability to translate scale into profitable growth. Backed by a 
deep leadership bench and disciplined capital allocation, the 
Company continues to strengthen its position across global 
gaming markets while maintaining financial resilience.
As Nazara enters its next era, it is nurturing a globally 
relevant gaming operating system rooted in India, powered 
by intellectual property, execution excellence and scalable 
platform capabilities.
Unlocking   
The Next Level
The Company has built a diversified global gaming 
platform over the past two decades. Through disciplined 
acquisitions, strategic investments, and focused execution, 
the Company stands at the intersection of frontier 
content, technology and consumer engagement.

A NEW CHAPTER 
IN NAZARA’S 
EVOLUTION
Nazara Technologies is entering a 
new chapter of growth. Backed by 
a refreshed brand identity and a 
new headquarters, the Company 
is channeling renewed energy 
into the same enduring objective 
of crafting magical and engaging 
experiences for its consumers 
and building for long-term impact. 
REDEFINING NAZARA 
The refreshed identity reflects that the Company has evolved far beyond its origins. 
At the centre of the change is the new ‘N’ insignia, designed as a wand with three 
rising stars, representing the pillars that now define Nazara’s operating philosophy. 
Imagination 
lies at the heart of the first star, expressing Nazara’s aspiration 
to create experiences that bring magic and joy to players in an 
increasingly demanding world
Creation  
shines through the second star, marking Nazara’s transformation 
into a creator and owner of enduring franchises. Supported by 
a 100% IP-focused portfolio comprising more than 25 franchises 
and backed by AI-led development capabilities, the Company 
is building scalable intellectual property designed for long-term 
relevance
Expansion  
represented by the third star, reflects the scale and diversity of 
Nazara’s global ambitions. Today, more than 90% of the Company’s 
gaming revenue is generated from international markets, particularly 
the US and the UK

While gaming has become the principal growth engine, 
the Nazara identity is built to hold a broader platform. 
Alongside its core, high-margin gaming businesses, 
the Company also operates complementary assets 
in sports media and adtech. These assets give the 
platform breadth and flexibility, opening options for 
future value while letting management keep a sharp 
focus on pure-play gaming.
As part of this transformation, Nazara has relocated its 
registered office to Avighna House in Worli, Mumbai. 
More than a corporate address, the new headquarters 
serves as the cultural and operational centre for a 
business that is India-born yet global in reach and 
impact. It is the physical anchor for Nazara’s central 
vision as well as a few of its Centres of Excellence 
(CoEs), which build shared competencies across user 
acquisition, AI, data analytics, growth and product. 
These functions form the operating backbone of the 
Company’s studios and businesses across markets.
Under this new phase, Nazara’s direction is clear: to 
build a platform-first organisation with global relevance 
and a deep commitment to intellectual property. By 
bringing every acquired and owned franchise onto 
a common operating framework powered by 
the CoEs and across-the-board, thoughtful 
integration of AI, Nazara is unlocking operating 
leverage and creating compounding value 
across its portfolio. 
With a diverse presence spanning India, Rest of 
Asia, Africa, North America, and Europe.  
The Company today operates on a far larger 
stage than ever before. Its operating leverage is 
real, and it is compounding.

ABOUT NAZARA TECHNOLOGIES 
BUILDING AN INTEGRATED  
GLOBAL GAMING PLATFORM
ABOUT NAZARA TECHNOLOGIES 
Nazara Technologies (‘Nazara’, or ‘The Company’) has cemented its position as an India-born diversified 
gaming and interactive entertainment platform for the world, combining owned and licensed IPs, operating 
businesses, and shared functions to serve audiences across formats, markets, and age groups. 
As India’s only publicly listed gaming company, Nazara operates across key international markets through a diverse mix of studios, platforms, and businesses. Its presence spans high-engagement 
categories such as mobile gaming, PC and console publishing, offline entertainment, esports, sports media and digital advertising technology.
At the core of the platform is a portfolio of more than 25 owned and licensed franchises supported by Centres of Excellence (CoEs) across user acquisition, data analytics, AI, growth, and product. 
This model enables Nazara to strengthen existing IPs, scale new opportunities, and build differentiated experiences for global audiences. The Company’s strong platform strategy translated into 
record financial performance during FY 2025-26, reinforcing the scalability and strength of its business model.

PLAYING IN 
STRUCTURALLY 
STRONG MARKETS 
From cricket fans and outdoor entertainment 
enthusiasts in India to young learners, casual 
gaming lovers and narrative-gaming players in North 
America and Europe, Nazara is building a globally 
admired gaming platform from India. More than 90% 
of its gaming revenue now comes from international 
markets, particularly from the US and the UK.  
GLOBAL PRESENCE 
India: High-Growth Opportunity
India continues to serve as the foundation of Nazara’s platform and the home 
of several flagship assets. The Company has built category-leading franchises 
such as World Cricket Championship (WCC), the world’s largest cricket simulation 
game, alongside operating experiential entertainment brands including 
SMAAASH and Funky Monkeys. With over 500 million mobile gamers, India 
remains the world’s largest market by downloads and offers a large monetisation 
opportunity. Through initiatives such as Nazara ID, the Company is building a 
direct network targeting 50 million to 100 million gamers.
United Kingdom and Europe:  
Home to Multiple Nazara Subsidiaries
The UK and Europe represent key mobile gaming, PC-Console gaming and adtech 
businesses within Nazara’s global ecosystem. The UK serves as the headquarters 
for Curve Games, Fusebox Games and Space & Time, while the proposed addition 
of Spain-based Bluetile Games strengthens the Company’s presence in casual 
social gaming. From a consumer lens too, several gaming businesses, including 
Kiddopia, Fusebox Games, Curve Games, C.A.T.S. and King of Thieves, count the UK 
and Europe among their most strategic markets.
North America: The Highest-ARPU Market
North America anchors some of Nazara’s most valuable franchises and 
subscription-led businesses. Kiddopia, Animal Jam, and its narrative-driven titles, 
including Love Island and Big Brother, have established a category-leading 
presence in the region. Sports media platforms Sportskeeda and Pro Football 
Network further strengthen the Company’s presence in the US. In FY 2025-26, 
the US accounted for more than 50% of Nazara’s gaming revenue, reflecting the 
Company’s focus on premium, high-value markets.

DEAR 
STAKEHOLDERS, 
Twenty-six years ago, Nazara was founded on a simple idea: 
a globally relevant gaming company could be built from 
India. Through sustained investment, disciplined acquisitions 
and a deepening commitment to owned intellectual property, 
that idea has grown into India’s most diversified gaming 
and interactive entertainment platform. FY 2025-26 was an 
important step in that evolution, deepening both the scale 
of the business and the foundations of its future growth.
What encouraged us most this year was not the financial 
performance alone, but the quality and durability of the 
progress behind it. Gaming contributed nearly 90% of EBITDA, 
the clearest sign yet of a sharper strategic focus and Nazara 
settling into its identity as a gaming-first global platform.
The global gaming industry is now valued at approximately 
US$ 224.7 billion. Behind those figures is a simple fact: 
games have become part of the daily lives of billions of 
people. Gaming is today the world’s largest entertainment 
category by both revenue and time spent, and it continues 
to expand across demographics, devices, and geographies.
Asia remains the largest regional market by revenue, 
supported by high engagement, mature platforms, and 
strong digital adoption. The forces reshaping the industry, 
though, are structural. AI is transforming game development, 
enabling AI-native studios to build, iterate, and scale content 
at a speed that was not possible before. Platform-agnostic 
distribution, built on cloud infrastructure and cross-device 
play, is dissolving the old boundaries between mobile, PC, 
and console gaming. Intellectual property has become one 
of the industry’s most durable sources of value. Franchises 
with loyal communities, recurring engagement, and long 
shelf life now take an outsized share of the economics.
India’s gaming market is changing at a scale and pace few 
others can match. The shift away from real-money gaming 
towards skill-based, casual and mid-core formats is creating 
a more stable, investment-friendly environment. Clearer 
regulation has given both domestic and international investors 
greater confidence. Telecom operators, hyperscalers, and 
state governments are investing across infrastructure, content, 
and talent, laying the groundwork for long-term growth.
Against this backdrop, Nazara continued to build the 
foundations of its next phase of growth. The proposed 
acquisition of Bluetile Games (including BestPlay Systems) 
adds not only scale but also AI-native development 
capabilities, advanced monetisation systems, and 
a large, active user base, strengthening the way 
the Company builds and operates its games.
We also continued to institutionalise our CoEs across User 
Acquisition, Data Analytics, AI, Growth, and Product. These 
shared functions give every business a common operating 
framework so that collective expertise, stronger execution, and 
better operating leverage flow across the portfolio. As more 
of our intellectual property comes into this framework, the 
benefits of scale and collaboration should become clearer still.
As the Board considers Nazara’s longer-term direction, 
three priorities stand out. The first is to deepen integration 
across the portfolio, so that shared functions and 
cross-group synergies are fully realised. The second 
is to drive operating leverage by scaling common 
infrastructure and the CoEs across our businesses. 
The third is to keep capital allocation disciplined while 
retaining the flexibility to invest where it strengthens 
the platform and builds long-term shareholder value.
The strength of FY 2025-26 came from the balance between 
ambition and discipline. FY 2026-27 will be a year of 
integration, execution, and scale. The planned full integration 
of Bluetile Games, the continued maturation of our existing 
mobile gaming portfolio and the steady expansion of the 
offline gaming portfolio give us a sound base to build on. We 
will continue integrating AI-native development capabilities 
across the broader portfolio, pursue cross-portfolio synergies 
through Nazara ID and shared user acquisition infrastructure, 
and maintain a disciplined, performance-linked approach 
to capital deployment. The foundations established over 
the past several years are increasingly positioned to 
compound at scale, as the Company enters its next era. 
I would like to thank our Board of Directors for their 
guidance and governance, our leadership teams for their 
commitment and execution, and our employees around 
the world for their creativity, passion, and dedication. I 
would also like to thank our partners and shareholders 
for their continued trust and support. We remain 
committed to building Nazara for generations to come. 
Warm regards,
Vikash Mittersain

DEAR 
STAKEHOLDERS, 
FY 2025-26 was an important milestone in Nazara 
Technologies’ evolution into a gaming-first global platform. 
Over the years, the Company has built a diversified 
portfolio spanning mobile gaming, PC and console 
publishing, offline gaming, and a few adjacencies. 
The strength of this platform-first approach shone through 
clearly this year, in both financial performance and the 
operating links that now run between the businesses. 
India offers a favourable environment for building digital-
first businesses. With internet access widening fast, rising 
smartphone adoption, and a mobile-native young population, 
the country is emerging both as a large consumption market 
and as a growing centre for content creation and innovation. 
Consumer tastes are shifting steadily towards immersive, 
interactive entertainment. Gaming sits at the centre of this 
shift, and it increasingly overlaps with adjacent segments 
such as esports, live experiences, and streaming, widening 
engagement and opening new ways to monetise.
The Company delivered consolidated revenue of  
` 1,829 Crores and its highest-ever EBITDA of ` 255 Crores, 
up 66% over FY 2024-25. EBITDA margins strengthened to 
13.9%, and pre-tax operating cash flow rose to ` 213 Crores. 
These figures reflect the quality of the portfolio, disciplined 
execution, and the rising contribution of high-margin gaming 
businesses. Gaming contributed nearly 90% of EBITDA 
during the year, the clearest measure of how far that shift 
has gone. Today, more than 90% of gaming revenue comes 
from international markets, giving the Company both global 
scale and market diversity. This balanced footprint lets the 
Company pursue growth on several fronts while reducing 
its dependence on any single geography or platform.
FY 2025-26 also marked the maturing of the Company’s CoEs 
into a genuine platform infrastructure. Their shared functions 
are now embedded across the portfolio, creating operating 
leverage and speeding up value creation. The impact of this 
model became increasingly visible during the year. Kiddopia 
returned to subscriber growth, Animal Jam delivered strong 
margin expansion, and Fusebox scaled multiple narrative 
franchises at once. Human: Fall Flat crossed 58 million lifetime 
units globally, and Funky Monkeys expanded its footprint to 
20 operational centres. Across businesses, geographies, and 
formats, the portfolio proved resilient, scalable, and  
well-executed. Together, these functions are building a 
common operating system through which existing and newly 
acquired intellectual property can be scaled more effectively.
AI moved deeper across the game lifecycle. From 
development and content creation to user acquisition, 
analytics, and player engagement, AI is enhancing 
productivity, accelerating decision-making, and improving 
the Company’s ability to scale experiences and content 
at an unprecedented pace across markets.
The year’s defining move was the proposed acquisition of 
Bluetile Games (including BestPlay). Their integration takes 
Nazara closer to a platform where technology, data, AI 
and intellectual property work together to create a lasting, 
competitive edge. Today, Nazara has built a diversified 
presence across Asia, Africa, North America, and Europe. 
Its widening reach, shared functions, and growing portfolio 
of intellectual property place the Company to compete in 
some of the most attractive segments of the industry.
The global and the Indian gaming markets keep expanding, 
and Nazara’s global platform provides more opportunities 
to compound value over time. With a diversified portfolio 
spanning geographies, platforms, and generations, the 
Company remains committed to building a globally relevant 
gaming platform from India. It continues to evaluate acquisitions 
actively. Capital deployment remains guided by discipline 
and supported by the CoE playbook. The focus is on backing 
businesses and intellectual property where shared functions 
can speed growth and create long-term value. As of  
March 31, 2026, we maintained a consolidated total cash 
position of ` 735 Crores, giving us the flexibility to invest in high-
return opportunities without compromising shareholder value.
To our shareholders, partners, employees, and the wider 
gaming community, I extend my sincere gratitude for your 
trust and support. I remain confident in what lies ahead and 
excited about the possibilities FY 2026-27 opens up.
Warm regards,

GLOBAL GAMING INDUSTRY
The global gaming industry sustained its structural growth through the year, moving further 
into the mainstream of global entertainment. Valued at an estimated US$ 224.7 billion in 
CY 2026, the market is projected to reach US$ 352.6 billion by CY 2031, reflecting a CAGR 
of 9.43%. This growth rests on three reinforcing shifts: wider smartphone ownership, steadily 
improving internet infrastructure, and a decisive move in consumer taste towards live-service 
and always-connected forms of play. Mobile gaming remains the dominant format, owing 
to its affordability, accessibility, and broad consumer reach. Advances in cloud gaming and 
streaming technologies are reducing dependence on high-end consoles and PCs and bringing 
the category within reach of a far wider audience. Asia-Pacific remains the largest regional 
market, anchored by its deep mobile user base and high rate of digital adoption, while rising 
investment in the Middle East and cloud-led expansion across Latin America are adding fresh 
sources of growth to the global market.
(Source: https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/global-gaming-market)

KEY DRIVERS AND TRENDS
Rising Momentum in Mobile Gaming Monetisation
 In CY 2025, global in-app purchases (IAPs) showcased strong resilience despite macroeconomic 
uncertainties. This resilience reflected gaming publishers’ adoption of recurring monetisation 
models such as battle passes and seasonal content updates. Regional pricing strategies 
contributed to a 6% increase in average revenue per paying user in CY 2025. The expansion 
of 5G infrastructure across emerging markets such as India, Indonesia, and Brazil is enabling 
low-latency real-time multiplayer experiences on affordable smartphones, widening access to 
premium mobile gaming. Developers are also deploying ad-supported engagement models 
that allow users to unlock virtual rewards and cosmetic items through short advertising 
interactions. Collectively, these trends reinforce mobile gaming as the largest contributor to the 
global gaming industry.
5G-Enabled Cloud Gaming Adoption
Cloud gaming revenue reached US$ 1.4 billion in CY 2025 and is projected to surpass US$ 18 
billion by CY 2030. Telecom operators are deploying edge computing infrastructure to reduce 
latency and convert network upgrades into recurring entertainment-led revenue streams. 
Leading technology players continue to invest in proprietary data centre infrastructure to 
capture a greater share of the value chain. These facilities maintain the sub-30-millisecond

Growth in In-Game Advertising Revenues 
In-game advertising has become a significant revenue contributor within the global gaming 
industry. Its share of total gaming revenues rose from 25% in CY 2020 to 32.3% in CY 2024 
and is projected to reach 38.5% by CY 2029. This trend reflects the growing importance of 
advertising as a core monetisation stream for the industry. With rising user acquisition costs 
and tightening privacy restrictions affecting traditional targeting methods, advertising-based 
monetisation is becoming a key pillar for sustaining free-to-play business models and expanding 
the gaming user base.
Rising Engagement in Esports
The esports industry continues to grow rapidly, driven by rising internet penetration, expanding 
gaming audiences, and increasing investments from brands and advertisers. The global market 
was valued at US$ 2.40 billion in CY 2025 and is expected to reach US$ 10.30 billion by 
CY 2034. Growing Gen Z engagement, the rise of creator-led content platforms, and initiatives 
such as the Olympic Esports Games are further accelerating the mainstream adoption of 
esports worldwide.
(Source: https://www.imarcgroup.com/esports-market, https://www.grandviewresearch.com/
industry-analysis/fantasy-sports-market-report)
Enhancement in Immersive Technologies
The immersive technology market in gaming is in a transformative phase, marked by 
rapid advances in virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and mixed reality (MR). These 
technologies are reshaping the gaming landscape and giving players deeper engagement 
and interactivity. As developers increasingly integrate immersive elements into their games, 
demand for high-quality hardware and software continues to rise. 
(Source: https://www.marketresearchfuture.com/reports/immersive-technology-in-gaming-
industry-market-12131)
AI Accelerating Innovation across Gaming
Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming game development, player engagement, and 
monetisation models. Adoption is rising across generative AI-powered game creation tools, 
intelligent non-player characters (NPCs), and adaptive gameplay that personalises content based 
on player behaviour and interactions. This uptake extends to large AAA publishers and reflects 
the growing strategic importance of AI within the gaming industry. Players, particularly younger 
audiences, are increasingly receptive to AI-driven gameplay, immersive NPC interactions, and 
dynamically evolving storylines. As AI lowers development barriers and raises content output 
across the industry, the factors that set studios apart are changing. Differentiated intellectual 
property, strong player communities, and efficient customer acquisition are expected to 
become increasingly important competitive advantages.
(Source: https://www.bcg.com/publications/2025/video-gaming-report-2026-next-era-of-
growth, https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/global-gaming-market)
INDIAN GAMING INDUSTRY
The continued expansion of India’s digital infrastructure is providing a strong foundation for 
the growth of the gaming ecosystem. In CY 2025, the country recorded 1,022 million internet 
users and 877 million smartphone users, supporting a gaming community of approximately 
555 million users. Payer conversion remained stable at 25%, translating into nearly 139 million 
paying gamers. While the market witnessed a marginal contraction following the enactment 
of the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, which effectively eliminated 
real-money gaming, underlying consumer engagement remained robust. Notably, gaming 
represented only 8% of the top downloaded applications but contributed 36% of revenue 
generated by the top-grossing apps, with gamers spending nearly 4.5 times more than 
non-gamers.

rising gamer engagement and growing digital content consumption. The industry’s growth is 
driven by wider smartphone penetration, affordable mobile data plans, and rising disposable

Localisation and Regional Content
Localisation is emerging as a key growth driver for the Indian mobile gaming market, with 
developers increasingly adapting content to regional languages, cultural preferences, and 
local narratives. The availability of games in vernacular languages such as Hindi, Tamil, and 
Telugu is helping expand the addressable user base and deepen engagement across diverse 
demographics. Reflecting this trend, industry surveys indicate that nearly 70% of businesses 
associated with the Indian mobile gaming ecosystem viewed local language and culture-led 
content as a critical factor supporting market growth in CY 2025.
Growing Adoption of Cloud Gaming
Cloud gaming is gradually gaining traction in India, supported by improving network 
infrastructure and increasing smartphone capabilities. The rapid rollout of 5G services, with 
coverage extending to more than 99% of districts through over 4,62,000 base transceiver 
stations, is enabling seamless access to high-quality gaming experiences without the need for 
advanced hardware. At the same time, the entry of cloud gaming platforms is making premium 
content more accessible at lower upfront costs. This trend is expected to broaden access 
to immersive gaming experiences and drive adoption across tier-II and tier-III cities, further 
expanding the reach of the Indian mobile gaming market.

ABOUT NAZARA TECHNOLOGIES 
Nazara Technologies Limited (‘Nazara’ or ‘the Company’) is a diversified global gaming 
and interactive entertainment platform built on the ownership, development, and scaling of 
intellectual property. With a portfolio spanning mobile, PC, console, and location-based gaming 
formats, the Company creates long-term value by bringing together owned IPs, engaged 
communities, and data-driven publishing capabilities across geographies and demographics.

relevant platform for gaming and digital entertainment.

necessary approvals), World Cricket Championship, and Crash Arena Turbo Stars, among 
others, that cater to audiences across gamified learning, storyline-driven role-playing games, 
casual action games, and sports games genres. Mobile gaming remains the largest contributor 
to the Company’s gaming operations and continues to benefit from investments in content 
development, player engagement, and franchise expansion. The planned introduction of

In premium gaming, the Company has built a growing presence through Curve Games, its PC 
and console publishing arm. A portfolio of globally recognised titles such as Human: Fall Flat 
and Wobbly Life alongside an expanding release pipeline has widened Nazara’s international 
footprint and carried its platform mix beyond mobile gaming.
Beyond digital gaming, Nazara owns and operates immersive offline entertainment businesses 
through Funky Monkeys and SMAAASH. These businesses extend the Company’s reach to 
audiences across physical and experiential settings, complementing its broader gaming 
portfolio. The continued expansion of Funky Monkeys and the strategic repositioning of 
SMAAASH extend its interactive entertainment across multiple consumer touchpoints.
Outside its core gaming businesses, in esports and pop culture, NODWIN Gaming brings 
together players, creators, fans, and brands around competitive gaming events and community-
led, youth lifestyle-focused experiences. Through marquee properties such as DreamHack, 
NH7 Weekender and Comic Con India, NODWIN has extended its reach across domestic 
and international markets, helping move esports and youth entertainment further into the 
mainstream. Alongside these businesses sit Nazara’s adtech operations, led by Datawrkz and 
Space & Time. Together, they provide technology-led digital marketing solutions and products 
that sharpen performance marketing for external clients and the wider Nazara group alike.
As the portfolio has grown in scale and complexity, Nazara has strengthened its operating 
framework through specialised Centres of Excellence (CoEs) focused on User Acquisition, 
Data Analytics, Growth, and Product Management. These shared capabilities drive operational 
efficiency, support knowledge transfer across businesses, and improve customer acquisition, 
engagement, and monetisation. The growing use of AI-driven tools in development and 
operational workflows is lifting productivity and accelerating innovation across the Company. 
Reflecting this evolution, Nazara recently introduced a refreshed brand identity under 
the positioning line ‘Enter. Magic.’, signalling its focus on building an integrated gaming OS 
(operating system) to deliver cutting-edge immersive, engaging gaming experiences to its 
global audiences.
Nazara continues to pursue growth through both organic expansion and strategic acquisitions. 
The addition of Bluetile Games (acquisition pending a Spanish regulatory approval) strengthens 
the Company’s casual and social gaming portfolio and elevates its AI-native gaming capabilities 
even further. Together with initiatives such as the development of the Nazara ID platform and 
a growing pipeline of franchise-led opportunities, these investments position the Company to 
deepen consumer engagement. They also support the creation of sustainable long-term value 
across the global gaming and interactive entertainment market, from India.

Curve Games 
In FY 2025-26, Curve Games delivered revenues of ` 260.7 Crores and EBITDA of ` 101.3 
Crores, translating into a robust EBITDA margin of 38.9%. The business maintained strong 
momentum through the year, supported by the enduring performance of its established 
franchises and a healthy pipeline of new releases. The strong cash generation enabled the 
platform to accelerate title signings and strengthen its publishing capabilities across premium 
PC and console gaming.
Curve’s flagship title, Human: Fall Flat, continued to demonstrate its evergreen appeal, 
surpassing 58 million lifetime units sold globally, with more than 2 million units added during 
FY 2025-26. Wobbly Life also crossed 2 million lifetime units, aided by strong traction on 
Nintendo Switch 1 since the launch in FY 2025-26. Meanwhile, For The King II recorded its 
strongest sales performance since launch, supported by the Fallen Oaths expansion.
The studio continued to deepen its publishing pipeline with the release of Wax Heads and 
upcoming titles including Sovereign Tower, Dragon Shelter, and Badlands Crew, the latter 
hitting the Top 10 charts on Steam. Going forward, Curve is targeting a faster release cadence, 
with five to six new titles expected across FY 2026-27 and FY 2027-28.

multi-IP portfolio and its contribution of ~27% to the Company’s gaming revenue underscore its 
growing strategic importance.
Curve Games
Curve Games delivered a strong breakout performance in FY 2025-26, its first full year of 
consolidation into Nazara. Revenue reached ` 261 Crores driven by steady monetisation of its 
PC and console back-catalogue. EBITDA stood at ` 101 Crores, reflecting a high-margin profile 
supported by efficient publishing operations and sustained IP performance. The studio has 
quickly emerged as a key profitability driver within Nazara’s global gaming portfolio.
Funky Monkeys
Funky Monkeys delivered strong growth in FY 2025-26, with revenue rising to ` 23 Crores 
versus its prior reported base. Growth was supported by rapid expansion across key Indian 
cities under a scalable, playbook-led offline entertainment model. EBITDA stood at ` 12 Crores, 
reflecting a high-margin operating structure driven by efficient centre-level economics and 
improved utilisation. The business continues to strengthen its position within Nazara’s offline 
entertainment portfolio, supported by disciplined expansion and consistent unit profitability.
SMAAASH
SMAAASH delivered a stable performance in FY 2025-26 following its consolidation into 
Nazara from June 6, 2025. Revenue of ` 76 Crores was supported by steady operational 
recovery and improved utilisation across centres. EBITDA stood at ` 15 Crores, reflecting cost 
optimisation and early stabilisation efforts ahead of the planned ‘SMAAASH 2.0’ relaunch.

Others
Datawrkz (including Space & Time)
Datawrkz, along with its UK subsidiary Space & Time, delivered steady growth in FY 2025-26, 
with revenue rising to ` 454 Crores from ` 346 Crores in FY 2024-25. EBITDA increased to ` 26 
Crores from ` 20 Crores in FY 2024-25, up 32% year-on-year, supported by improving revenue 
mix and operational efficiencies. The year marked a shift towards higher-margin, tech-enabled 
offerings, strengthening the long-term profitability of Nazara’s adtech segment.
Sportskeeda (Absolute Sports)
The Sportskeeda platform faced headwinds in FY 2025-26 following a Google March Core 
Update that impacted US organic traffic. Revenue came in at ` 147 Crores. EBITDA stood at 
` 18 Crores, reflecting continued operational efficiency despite top-line pressure. Within the 
Absolute Sports portfolio, other properties such as Pro Football Network (PFN) and PrimeTimer 
showcased rapid and profitable growth through the fiscal year. PFN recorded its best-ever 
annual performance since acquisition, with the Sportskeeda operating playbook driving a 28% 
EBITDA margin, the highest in the property’s history. 
NODWIN Gaming
NODWIN Gaming staged a remarkable turnaround in FY 2025-26, with revenue rising to 
` 658 Crores from ` 524 Crores in FY 2024-25, supported by a fuller events calendar and 
continued organic expansion. EBITDA improved sharply to a profit of ` 21 Crores from a loss 
of ` 14 Crores in FY 2024-25, marking a significant operational recovery and margin reset. 
FY 2025-26 also marked a major structural shift, as NODWIN moved to an associate company 
following its de-subsidiarisation from Nazara Technologies.

OUTLOOK
The global gaming industry is moving into a new growth phase, shaped by wider smartphone 
and internet access, evolving models of player engagement, and the spread of AI through 
development and monetisation. In India, favourable demographics, expanding digital 
infrastructure, widespread 5G adoption, and a growing preference for skill-based and non-
RMG formats continue to underpin the industry’s long-term outlook.
Nazara is well placed to benefit from these structural tailwinds. In FY 2025-26, the Company 
delivered its highest-ever EBITDA, reflecting the increasing contribution of its high-margin 
gaming businesses and the strength of a diversified IP portfolio. The year marked a pivotal shift, 
with gaming now contributing 59% of revenue and 90% of EBITDA. Continued investment in 
CoE across user acquisition, AI, data analytics, and product management has further sharpened 
execution and improved operating leverage across the portfolio.
The proposed acquisition of Bluetile and BestPlay is a defining step in Nazara’s global growth. 
With the full-year integration of Curve Games, the expansion of Animal Jam, and the scaling 
of offline brands such as Funky Monkeys and SMAAASH, the Company is steadily building 
a multi-format gaming business of global reach. Integrating AI-driven capabilities and shared 
technology platforms is expected to unlock further efficiencies and accelerate innovation 
across the Company’s businesses.
Looking ahead, Nazara will continue to deepen monetisation across its owned IPs, strengthen 
cross-portfolio synergies, and pursue disciplined inorganic growth. Backed by a strong liquidity 
position, healthy cash generation, and a proven acquisition and integration framework, the 
Company is well placed to scale sustainably. Nazara’s long-term ambition is to build one of 
the world’s most valuable integrated gaming platforms to originate from India, with a portfolio 
spanning geographies, platforms, and generations.

INTERNAL CONTROL SYSTEMS 
The Company has implemented internal financial controls commensurate to the scale and 
complexity of its operations. These controls, guided by defined policies and procedures, 
ensure operational discipline, asset security, and timely detection of anomalies. The Audit 
Committee conducts regular reviews to assess their effectiveness. During the year, M/s. MAKK 
& Co., Chartered Accountants, conducted an internal audit, followed by reviews to ensure 
implementation of key findings. The Board of Directors ensures adequate controls are in place 
for accurate and compliant financial reporting.
HUMAN RESOURCES
Nazara continues to build its human capital through stronger leadership, enhancement, 
centralised capability building, and structured workforce governance, supporting its global IP-
led growth.
The Company has reinforced its leadership team with experienced professionals, including Rohit 
Sharma as Executive Director and Rod Cousens as Strategic Advisor. It has also strengthened 
leadership across key subsidiaries such as Kiddopia, Sportskeeda, and Datawrkz.
Nazara has established CoEs across user acquisition, data, product and content, and offline 
gaming to improve efficiency, standardisation, and scalability across its gaming portfolio.
Overall, the Company’s HR strategy focuses on attracting, retaining, and developing specialised 
talent through structured policies, learning initiatives, and strong governance frameworks 
aligned with its long-term growth objectives. Nazara aims to maintain an employee attrition rate 
below 15% and Director-level attrition at 0%.

BUSINESS OVERVIEW
Nazara Technologies is India’s only publicly listed gaming company. Its key businesses include 
Curve Games, Bluetile Games (pending necessary approvals), Kiddopia, Animal Jam, Fusebox 
Games (Love Island, Big Brother, Bigg Boss), World Cricket Championship and Sportskeeda, 
along with offline gaming businesses such as Funky Monkeys and Smaaash Entertainment. 
Nazara also operates Datawrkz, a digital ad tech business and Absolute Sports, a sports media 
platform. With presence in India, North America, and other global markets, Nazara is building a 
global gaming platform with strong IP, publishing, and operating capabilities.
During the financial year ended on March 31, 2026, on a Standalone basis the Company has 
registered a turnover of ` 7,384 Lakhs as against ` 3,442 Lakhs in the previous year. The

Description of the ESOP Schemes
The Company has formulated and implemented Employee Stock Option Schemes viz. Nazara Technologies Employee Stock Option Scheme 2023 and Nazara Technologies Employee Stock 
Option Scheme 2025, the details of which are provided as follows:

aggregate number of Equity Shares to be issued under ESOP 2023, upon exercise, shall not exceed 1,58,730 Equity Shares at such price and on such terms and conditions as may be fixed or 
determined by the Board. ESOP 2023 is in compliance with the SEBI SBEB Regulations.
ESOP 2025: The Company adopted ESOP 2025, pursuant to resolutions passed by the Board and Shareholders dated November 12, 2025, and January 15, 2026, respectively. The purpose 
of ESOP 2025 is to reward eligible employees of our Company (as defined in ESOP 2025) for their performance in our Company and to share the wealth created by the Company with them. 
The aggregate number of Equity Shares to be issued under ESOP 2025, upon exercise, shall not exceed 18,52,325 Equity Shares at such price and on such terms and conditions as may be 
fixed or determined by the Board. ESOP 2025 is in compliance with the SEBI SBEB Regulations.
There is no change in ESOP 2023 and ESOP 2025 Schemes and the Schemes are in compliance with the SEBI SBEB Regulations.

I.	
COMPANY’S PHILOSOPHY ON CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
Effective Corporate Governance practice is about commitment to values, ethical business 
conduct and constitutes strong fundamentals on which a successful commercial enterprise 
is built to last. The process ensures that these practices are utilised in a manner that meets 
stakeholders’ aspirations and societal expectations. It is this conviction that has led the 
Company to make strong corporate governance values integral to its operations. The 
Company has established systems and procedures based on the overview and strategic 
counsel of the Board and it is fully equipped to discharge its responsibilities and to provide 
the management the strategic direction it needs.
We believe that good Corporate Governance is much more than just complying with legal 
and regulatory requirements in letter. Keeping in view the above, your Company pledges 
to uphold the legacy of adhering to the law not only in letter but in spirit also and hereby 
acknowledges the responsibility and faith reposed by all the stakeholders.

prescribed under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and

II.	
BOARD OF DIRECTORS
The main role and responsibility of the Board is that of trusteeship, protecting and 
enhancing the value of all the stakeholders. The Company believes that good Corporate 
Governance is a basic and fundamental requirement and condition precedent for strong 
over-all performance. The Board Members, Executive Management and the employees 
of the Company are brand ambassadors of its image and vision, who collectively act 
to maintain the highest standard of Corporate Governance with a responsibility to meet 
the expectations of the stakeholders. We firmly believe that the Board of the Company 
should have an appropriate mix of Executive, Non-Executive and Independent Directors 
to maintain its Independence, and to separate its functions of governance with that of 
management. Your Board represents a confluence of varied skills, experience and 
expertise from diverse backgrounds. The Directors possess requisite qualifications, 
experience and expertise in their respective functional areas, which enables them to 
discharge their responsibilities and provide effective leadership and act as a mentor 
to the management of the Company. The Board also provides direction and exercises 
appropriate control to ensure that the Company is managed in a manner that fulfils and 
boosts the morale of the stakeholders, strategic investors and the public at large.

B.	
Process of appointment of a Director
The appointment of Directors in your Company is recommended by the Nomination, 
Remuneration and Compensation Committee ("NRC"), approved by the Board of 
Directors and subsequently approved by the Shareholders in accordance with the 
provisions of the Act and the Listing Regulations.
Independent Directors are appointed for a term of up to 05 (five) consecutive years 
and are eligible for re‑appointment for a further term of up to 05 (five) consecutive 
years, subject to approval of the Shareholders by way of a special resolution and 
their continued compliance with the independence criteria prescribed under the Act 
and the Listing Regulations.
Independent Directors are not liable to retire by rotation. Whole‑time Directors, 
including the Managing Director and Executive Director(s), are appointed for a term 
of up to 05 (five) years as approved by the Shareholders and may be re‑appointed 
based on the recommendation of the NRC and the Board.
In accordance with the provisions of the Act and the Articles of Association of the 
Company, the requisite number of Directors, other than Independent Directors, are 
liable to retire by rotation at every Annual General Meeting.

I.	
Board Procedure:
The Board meetings are generally held at the registered office of the Company in 
Mumbai. The Company Secretary, in consultation with the Chairman of the Board and 
Joint Managing Director & CEO, prepares and finalises the agenda of the Board meetings. 
For all major agenda items, relevant and comprehensive background information is 
provided along with the agenda well in advance of the date of the Board Meeting(s) 
to enable the Board members to take informed decisions. Any Board member may, in 
consultation with the Chairman and with the consent of all the Independent Directors 
present at the meeting, propose any matter for discussion and consideration at the 
Board meeting. The Senior Management Personnel are invited to the Board meetings to 
make presentations on relevant issues or provide necessary insights into the operations/
working of the Company and corporate strategies, from time to time.
The Board/Committee meetings are pre-scheduled and a tentative annual calendar 
of the Board and Committee meetings is circulated to all the Directors in advance 
in order to facilitate them to plan their schedule and ensure participation in the 
meetings. However, in case of special and urgent business needs, the Board’s 
approval is taken by passing resolution by circulation, as permitted by law, which 
is noted and confirmed in the subsequent Board Meeting. During the financial year 
2025-26, most of the meetings of the Board were held through video conference in 
accordance with the provisions of law.
The Company has followed the mandatory requirements of Secretarial Standard - 1 
and 2 issued by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India ("ICSI") and guidelines/
circulars issued by Ministry of Corporate Affairs ("MCA"), from time to time in relation 
to conduct of meetings of the Board, its committees and general meetings through 
Video Conferencing and/or Other Audio-Visual Means.
All relevant information required to be placed before the Board as per the Listing 
Regulations is considered and taken on record/approved by the Board. The Board 
reviews and guides the Company in strategic matters, risk management and oversees 
the process of disclosure and communications to maintain the highest standards of 
ethical conduct and integrity. Additionally, the Board periodically reviews Compliance 
Reports in respect of various laws and regulations applicable to the Company.
	
J.	
Independent Directors’ Meeting & Board Evaluation Process
Regulation 25 of the Listing Regulations, Schedule IV of the Act and the Rules made 
thereunder mandate the Independent Directors of the Company to hold at least 
one meeting in a year, without the attendance of non-independent directors and 
members of the management. The main objective of such meetings is to evaluate 
the performance of the chairman, the non-independent directors and the overall 
performance of the board and its committees by the independent directors.
At the said meeting, apart from conducting performance evaluation, the Independent 
Directors assessed the quality, quantity and timeliness of flow of information between 
the Company’s management and the Board, that is necessary for the Board to 
perform their duties effectively and reasonably.
The parameters for evaluation of performance of the Board and Board Committees 
includes the structure and composition, contents of agenda for the meeting, quality 
and timeliness of information provided, decision-making process and review thereof,

CS Sandhya Malhotra (ICSI Membership No. FCS 6715), Partner of M/s. Manish Ghia & Associates, Company Secretaries, Mumbai, was appointed as the Scrutiniser for the aforesaid Postal 
Ballot processes to scrutinise the voting conducted through electronic means only (remote e-voting) in a fair and transparent manner.
No Special Resolution is proposed to be conducted through postal ballot as on date of this Annual Report.
Procedure adopted for Postal Ballot:
Pursuant to and in compliance with the Sections 108 and 110 and all other applicable provisions, if any, of the Act, read with Rule 20 and Rule 22 of the Companies (Management and 
Administration) Rules, 2014 (“the Rules”), Regulation 44 of the Listing Regulations (including any statutory modification(s) or re-enactment(s) of the Act or Rules or Listing Regulations, as 
the case may be, for the time being in force), General Circulars issued by the MCA (hereinafter collectively referred to as “MCA Circulars”) and the Securities and Exchange Board of India 
Circular (hereinafter collectively referred to as “SEBI Circulars”) in this regard, the Postal Ballot Notice was sent to the Members of the Company for seeking their consent on resolutions 
set out in the postal ballot notice, only by way of remote electronic voting (“e-voting”).
The Company had engaged the services of Central Depository Services (India) Limited (“CDSL”) to provide e-voting facility to the Members of the Company to exercise their votes 
electronically and vote on the resolutions through the e-voting service facility arranged by CDSL. Members whose names appears in the Register of Members/ List of Beneficial Owners 
for postal ballot, as on the respective cut-off dates, were eligible to cast their votes on the resolutions set out in the respective Notices.
The Scrutinisers submitted their reports to the Company Secretary based on the authorisation by the Chairman of the Company, after the completion of scrutiny and the consolidated 
results of the voting by Postal Ballot were then announced by the Company Secretary.
The voting results pursuant to Regulation 44(3) of the Listing Regulations and Section 108 of the Act read with the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014, and 
Scrutiniser’s Report on remote e-voting were placed on the Company’s website at https://investors.nazara.com/company-announcements and were available on the website of the Stock 
Exchanges and CDSL.

To the Members of Nazara Technologies Limited
Report on the Audit of the Standalone Financial Statements
OPINION
We have audited the accompanying standalone financial statements of Nazara Technologies 
Limited (“the Company”), which comprise the Balance Sheet as at March 31, 2026, and the 
Statement of Profit and Loss (including Other Comprehensive loss), the Statement of Changes 
in Equity and the Statement of Cash Flows for the year then ended, and notes to the standalone 
financial statements, including material accounting policy information and other explanatory 
information (hereinafter referred to as the “standalone financial statements”).
In our opinion and to the best of our information and according to the explanations given to us, 
the aforesaid standalone financial statements give the information required by the Companies 
Act, 2013 (“the Act’) in the manner so required and give a true and fair view in conformity with 
the Indian Accounting Standards prescribed under section 133 of the Act read with Companies 
(Indian Accounting Standards) Rules, 2015, as amended (“Ind AS”) and other accounting 
principles generally accepted in India, of the state of affairs of the Company as at March 31, 
2026, and its loss (including other comprehensive loss), changes in equity and its cash flows 
for the year ended on that date.
BASIS FOR OPINION
We conducted our audit of the standalone financial statements in accordance with the 
Standards on Auditing (SAs) specified under section 143(10) of the Act. Our responsibilities 
under those SAs are further described in the Auditor’s Responsibilities for the Audit of the 
standalone Financial Statements section of our report. We are independent of the Company in 
accordance with the Code of Ethics issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India 
together with the ethical requirements that are relevant to our audit of the standalone financial 
statements under the provisions of the Act and the Rules thereunder, and we have fulfilled our 
other ethical responsibilities in accordance with these requirements and the Code of Ethics. 
We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide 
a basis for our opinion.
EMPHASIS OF MATTER
We draw attention to Note 5 of the accompanying standalone financial Statement, which 
describes the recognition of impairment loss of ` 98,894 Lakhs on investment in one of the 
associate company due to prohibition in offering of online money games pursuant to the 
enactment of the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025
Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.
KEY AUDIT MATTERS
Key audit matters are those matters that, in our professional judgment, were of most significance 
in our audit of the standalone financial statements of the current period. These matters were 
addressed in the context of our audit of the standalone financial statements as a whole, and in 
forming our opinion thereon, and we do not provide a separate opinion on these matters. We 
have determined the matters described below to be the key audit matters to be communicated 
in our report.
IMPAIRMENT ASSESSMENT OF INVESTMENTS IN AND LOANS TO SUBSIDIARIES 
AND ASSOCIATES
As described in Note 5 to the standalone financial statements, carrying value (net of 
impairment) of investment in subsidiaries and associates as at March 31, 2026 is ` 1,34,038 
Lakhs respectively. Further, the Company has given loans amounting to ` 25,143 Lakhs as at 
March 31, 2026 to such entities as given in note 6 to standalone financial statements.
The management has noted impairment indicators in few of these entities as Company’s share in 
net asset is lower than carrying value of investment as at March 31, 2026. In view of the above, the 
Management of the Company has carried out an impairment testing for these identified investments 
using discounted cash flow model. Key assumptions used in management’s assessment include 
estimates of future financial performance, terminal value and discount rates, amongst others, 
as attributable to such subsidiaries and associate. Based on the management’s assessment, 
impairment loss of ` 1,07,896 Lakhs has been recognized on investment in subsidiaries and 
associates as at March 31, 2026. Further, the management has recorded an impairment of 
` 33 Lakhs towards loans given to an entity as at March 31, 2026.

Report on the Internal Financial Controls with reference to standalone financial statements 
under Clause (i) of Sub-section 3 of Section 143 of the Companies Act, 2013 (“the Act”)
OPINION
We have audited the internal financial controls with reference to standalone financial statements 
of Nazara Technologies Limited (“the Company”) as of March 31, 2026 in conjunction with our 
audit of the standalone financial statements of the Company for the year ended on that date.
In our opinion, and to the best of our information and according to the explanations given 
to us, the Company has, in all material respects, an adequate internal financial controls with 
reference to standalone financial statements and such internal financial controls with reference 
to standalone financial statements were operating effectively as at March 31, 2026 based on 
the internal financial controls with reference to financial statements criteria established by the 
Company considering the essential components of internal control stated in the Guidance 
Note on Audit of Internal Financial Controls Over Financial Reporting (the “Guidance Note”) 
issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (‘ICAI’).
MANAGEMENT’S AND BOARD OF DIRECTOR’S RESPONSIBILITIES FOR INTERNAL 
FINANCIAL CONTROLS
The Company’s Management and the Board of Directors are responsible for establishing and 
maintaining internal financial controls based on the internal financial controls with reference to 
financial statements criteria established by the Company considering the essential components 
of internal control stated in the Guidance Note issued by the ICAI. These responsibilities include 
the design, implementation and maintenance of adequate internal financial controls that were 
operating effectively for ensuring the orderly and efficient conduct of its business, including 
adherence to Company’s policies, the safeguarding of its assets, the prevention and detection 
of frauds and errors, the accuracy and completeness of the accounting records, and the timely 
preparation of reliable financial information, as required under the Act.
ANNEXURE C
AUDITOR’S RESPONSIBILITY
Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company’s internal financial controls with 
reference to standalone financial statements based on our audit. We conducted our audit 
in accordance with the Guidance Note issued by the ICAI and the Standards on Auditing 
prescribed under section 143(10) of the Act, to the extent applicable to an audit of internal 
financial controls with reference to standalone financial statements. Those Standards and 
the Guidance Note require that we comply with ethical requirements and plan and perform 
the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether adequate internal financial controls 
with reference to standalone financial statements was established and maintained and if such 
controls operated effectively in all material respects.
Our audit involves performing procedures to obtain audit evidence about the adequacy of the 
internal financial controls with reference to standalone financial statements and their operating 
effectiveness. Our audit of internal financial controls with reference to standalone financial 
statements included obtaining an understanding of internal financial controls with reference 
to standalone financial statements, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, and 
testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on 
the assessed risk. The procedures selected depend on the auditor’s judgement, including 
the assessment of the risks of material misstatement of the standalone financial statements, 
whether due to fraud or error.
We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained, is sufficient and appropriate to provide 
a basis for our audit opinion on the Company’s internal financial controls with reference to 
standalone financial statements.
MEANING OF INTERNAL FINANCIAL CONTROLS WITH REFERENCE TO FINANCIAL 
STATEMENTS
A company’s internal financial control with reference to financial statements is a process 
designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and 
the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally 
accepted accounting principles. A company’s internal financial control with reference to 
financial statements includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance 
of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and 
dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions

are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with 
generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company 
are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the 
company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of 
unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company’s assets that could have a material 
effect on the financial statements.
INHERENT LIMITATIONS OF INTERNAL FINANCIAL CONTROLS WITH REFERENCE TO 
FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
Because of the inherent limitations of internal financial controls with reference to financial 
statements, including the possibility of collusion or improper management override of controls, 
material misstatements due to error or fraud may occur and not be detected. Also, projections 
of any evaluation of the internal financial controls with reference to financial statements to 
future periods are subject to the risk that the internal financial control with reference to financial 
statements may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of 
compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.

(ii)	
Current versus non-current classification
The Company presents assets and liabilities in the balance sheet based on current/ 
non-current classification. An asset is treated as current when it is:
•	
Expected to be realised or intended to be sold or consumed in normal operating 
cycle
•	
Held primarily for the purpose of trading
•	
Expected to be realised in normal operating cycle or within twelve months after 
the reporting period or
•	
Cash or cash equivalents unless restricted from being exchanged or used to 
settle a liability for at least twelve months after the reporting period
All other assets are classified as non-current.
A liability is current when:
•

twelve months after the reporting period
•	
It is held primarily for the purpose of trading
•	
There is no unconditional right to defer the settlement of the liability for at least 
twelve months after the reporting period
All other liabilities are classified as non-current.
Deferred tax assets and liabilities are classified as non-current assets and liabilities.
The operating cycle is the time between the acquisition of assets for processing and 
their realisation in cash and cash equivalents. The Company has identified period of 
twelve months as its operating cycle.

The areas involving significant judgement and estimates are as follows:
	
a)	
Estimated useful life of property and equipment and intangible assets
The charge in respect of periodic depreciation/ amortisation is derived after 
determining an estimate of an asset’s expected useful life and the expected residual 
value at the end of its life. Management at the time the asset is acquired/ capitalised 
periodically, including at each financial year end, determines the useful lives and 
residual values of Company’s assets. The lives are based on historical experience 
with similar assets as well as anticipation of future events, which may affect their life, 
such as changes in technology.
Estimation of fair value of unlisted securities
The Company follows Ind AS 109 - Financial Instruments: to determine the fair value 
of its investment in equity instruments using market and income approaches. The 
market approach includes the use of financial metrics and ratios of comparable 
companies, such as revenue, earnings, comparable performance multiples, recent 
financial rounds and the level of marketability of the investments. The selection of 
comparable companies requires management judgment and is based on number 
of factors, including comparable company sises, growth rates and development 
stages. The income approach includes the use of discounted cash flow model, which 
requires significant estimates regarding the investees’ revenue, costs, and discount 
rates based on the risk profile of comparable companies. Estimates of revenue and 
costs are developed using available historical and forecasted data. These estimates 
may vary from the actual prices that would be achieved in an arm’s length transaction 
at the reporting date.
b)	
Impairment in carrying value of investments in subsidiaries and associates

Recognition of deferred tax assets
Deferred tax assets are recognised to the extent that it is probable that future 
taxable profit will be available against which the losses can be utilised. In assessing 
the probability, the Company considers whether the entity has sufficient taxable 
temporary differences, which will result in taxable amounts against which the unused 
tax losses or unused tax credits can be utilised before they expire. Significant 
management judgement is required to determine the amount of deferred tax assets 
that can be recognised, based upon the likely timing and the level of future taxable 
profits together with future tax planning strategies.

Interest income is recorded using the effective interest rate (‘EIR’) method. EIR is the

financial liability. Interest income is included under the head “finance income” in the 
statement of profit and loss account.

Subsequent measurement
For purposes of subsequent measurement, financial assets are classified in three 
broad categories:
•	
Financial assets at amortised cost
•	
Financial assets at fair value through other comprehensive income (FVOCI)
•	
Financial assets at fair value through profit and loss (FVTPL)
	
	
Financial assets at amortised cost
A Financial assets is measured at amortised cost (net of any write down for 
impairment) the asset is held to collect the contractual cash flows (rather than to sell 
the instrument prior to its contractual maturity to realise its fair value changes) and 
The contractual terms of the financial asset give rise on specified dates to cash flows 
that are solely payments of principal and interest (“SPPI”) on the principal amount 
outstanding.
Such financial assets are subsequently measured at amortised cost using the 
effective interest rate (EIR) method. Amortised cost is calculated by taking into 
account any discount or premium on acquisition and fees or costs that are an integral 
part of the EIR. The EIR amortisation is included in other income in the profit and loss. 
The losses arising from impairment are recognised statement of profit and loss. This 
category generally applies to trade and other receivables.
	
	
Financial asset at fair value through other comprehensive income (FVOCI)
A financial asset that meets the following two conditions is measured at fair value 
through other comprehensive income unless the asset is designated at fair value

which are not fair value through profit and loss and equity instruments recognised

lifetime ECLs at each reporting date, right from its initial recognition.
For recognition of impairment loss on other financial assets and risk exposure, the 
Company determines that whether there has been a significant increase in the credit 
risk since initial recognition. If credit risk has not increased significantly, 12-month 
ECL is used to provide for impairment loss. However, if credit risk has increased 
significantly, lifetime ECL is used.

over the expected life of a financial instrument. The 12-month ECL is a portion of the 
lifetime ECL which results from default events that are possible within 12 months after

instrument. However, in rare cases when the expected life of the financial 
instrument cannot be estimated reliably, then the entity is required to use the 
remaining contractual term of the financial instrument.

(ix)	 Impairment of non-financial assets
The Company assesses at each reporting date whether there is an indication that 
an asset may be impaired. If any indication exists, or when annual impairment testing 
for an asset is required, the Company estimates the asset’s recoverable amount. 
An asset’s recoverable amount is the higher of an asset’s or cash-generating unit’s 
(CGU) net selling price and its value in use. The recoverable amount is determined 
for an individual asset, unless the asset does not generate cash inflows that are 
largely independent of those from other assets or groups of assets. When the 
carrying amount of an asset or CGU exceeds its recoverable amount, the asset is 
considered impaired and is written down to its recoverable amount.
In assessing value in use, the estimated future cash flows are discounted to their 
present value using a pre-tax discount rate that reflects current market assessments 
of the time value of money and the risks specific to the asset. In determining fair 
value less costs of disposal, recent market transactions are taken into account. If no 
such transactions can be identified, an appropriate valuation model is used.
The impairment calculations are based on detailed budgets and forecast calculations 
for each of the Company’s CGUs covering a period of five years and applying a long-
term growth rate to project future cash flows after the fifth year. Impairment losses of 
operations are recognised in the statement of profit and loss.
At each reporting date if there is an indication that previously recognised impairment 
losses no longer exist or have decreased, the Company estimates the asset’s or 
CGU’s recoverable amount. A previously recognised impairment loss is reversed in 
the statement of profit and loss only to the extent of lower of its recoverable amount 
or carrying amount net of depreciation considering no impairment loss recognised in 
prior periods only if there has been a change in the assumptions used to determine 
the asset’s recoverable amount since the last impairment loss was recognised.

(xvii)	Fair value measurement
Fair value is the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a 
liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement 
date. The fair value measurement is based on the presumption that the transaction 
to sell the asset or transfer the liability takes place either:
•	
In the principal market for the asset or liability - or
•	
In the absence of a principal market, in the most advantageous market for the 
asset or liability.
The principal or the most advantageous market must be accessible by the Company.
The fair value of an asset or a liability is measured using the assumptions that market 
participants would use when pricing the asset or liability, assuming that market 
participants act in their economic best interest.
The Company uses valuation techniques that are appropriate in the circumstances 
and for which sufficient data are available to measure fair value, maximising the use 
of relevant observable inputs and minimising the use of unobservable inputs.
All assets and liabilities for which fair value is measured or disclosed in the 
standalone financial statement are categorised within the fair value hierarchy, 
described as follows, based on the lowest level input that is significant to the fair 
value measurement as a whole:
•	
Level 1 — Quoted (unadjusted) market prices in active markets for identical 
assets or liabilities
•	
Level 2 — Valuation techniques for which the lowest level input that is significant 
to the fair value measurement is directly or indirectly observable.
•	
Level 3 — Valuation techniques for which the lowest level input that is significant 
to the fair value measurement is unobservable
For the purpose of fair value disclosures, the Company has determined classes of 
financial assets and liabilities on the basis of the nature, characteristics and risks of 
the asset or liability and the level of the fair value hierarchy as explained above.

(xxi)	Foreign currency transactions and balances
	
	
i.	
Functional currency
	
The financial statements are presented in Indian Rupees (`), which is the 
functional currency of the Company and the currency of the primary economic 
environment in which the Company operates.
	
	
ii.	
Transactions and translations
	
Transactions in foreign currencies are initially recorded by the Company at 
its functional currency spot rates at the date the transaction first qualifies for 
recognition. Monetary assets and liabilities denominated in foreign currencies 
are translated at the functional currency spot rates of exchange at the reporting 
date. Exchange differences arising on settlement or translation of monetary 
items are recognised in profit or loss with the exception of the following: 
Exchange differences arising on monetary items that forms part of a 
reporting entity’s net investment in a foreign operation are recognised 
in profit or loss in the financial statement of the reporting entity. 
Non-monetary items that are measured in terms of historical cost in a foreign 
currency are translated using the exchange rates at the dates of the initial 
transactions. Non-monetary items measured at fair value in a foreign currency 
are translated using the exchange rates at the date when the fair value is 
determined. The gain or loss arising on translation of non-monetary items 
measured at fair value is treated in line with the recognition of the gain or loss 
on the change in fair value of the item (i.e., translation differences on items 
whose fair value gain or loss is recognised in other comprehensive income or 
profit or loss are also recognised in OCI or profit or loss, respectively).”
	
(xxii)	Standards issued but not yet effective
The Ministry of corporate Affairs (“”MCA””) notified amendments on May 07, 2025 and 
August 13, 2025 under the Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Amendment 
Rules, 2025 and the Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Second Amendment 
Rules, 2025, respectively, which is effective from annual reporting periods beginning 
on or after April 01, 2025.
	
(a)	
Amendment to Ind AS 7 and Ind AS 107 - Supplier Finance Arrangement:
The amendments to Ind AS 7 ‘Statement of Cash Flows’ and Ind AS 107 ‘Financial 
Instruments: Disclosures’ clarify the characteristics of supplier finance arrangements 
and require additional disclosures for such arrangements. The disclosure 
requirements in the amendments are intended to assist users of financial statements 
in understanding the effects of supplier finance arrangements on an entity’s liabilities, 
cash flows and exposure to liquidity risk.
The Company does not have any supplier finance arrangements during the reporting 
period.
	
(b)	 Amendment to Ind AS 1 - Classification of liabilities as current or non-current and 
non-current liabilities with covenants:
The amendment specifies the requirements for classifying liabilities as current or 
non-current in the balance sheet, and clarifies the following:
i)	
An entity’s right to defer settlement of a liability for at least twelve months after the 
reporting period must have substance and must exist at the end of the reporting 
period. The classification of a liability as current or non-current is unaffected by 
the likelihood that the entity will exercise its right to defer settlement.
ii)	
If an entity’s right to defer settlement of a liability is subject to covenants, such 
covenants affect whether that right exists at the end of the reporting period only 
if the entity is required to comply with the covenant on or before the end of the 
reporting period.
iii)	
In case of a liability that can be settled, at the option of the counterparty, by the 
transfer of the entity’s own equity instruments, such settlement terms do not 
affect the classification of the liability as current or non-current only if the option 
is classified as an equity instrument.

Amendment to Ind AS 1 ‘Presentation of Financial Statements’- Classification of

The amendment includes specific provisions that will take effect for reporting periods 
beginning on or after April 01, 2026, retrospectively, as outlined below:
a)

reporting date, then it shall be classified as current liability, if lender agreed after 
reporting period and before approval of financial statements to not demand

b)	
Classify as non-current liability, if lender agreed by end of reporting period to 
provide grace period ending at least 12 months after reporting period within 
which entity can rectify the breach provided lender does not demand immediate 
repayment.
c)	
Disclose information about the timing of settlement to understand the impact of 
the liability on the financial statements.

and SMAAASH Entertainment Private Limited has become a wholly owned subsidiary of 
the Company; and the Company has extended an inter-corporate loan for an amount of

The Company on June 26, 2025 has infused funds aggregating to US$ 300,000/- 
(equivalent to approx. ` 260 Lakhs) in Play Venture Fund III and US$ 250,000/- (equivalent 
to approx. ` 214 Lakhs) in Fund I, a series of F4 Ventures, LP, as a Limited Partner, by way

Further, Company on November 25, 2025 and February 10, 2026 has infused additional

On August 13, 2025, following shareholder approval at the Extraordinary General Meeting 
(EGM), the Company ceased to control NODWIN Gaming Private Limited (NODWIN). 
Accordingly, Investment in NODWIN is reclassified as an associate with effective from 
August 13, 2025.
G	
On August 21, 2025, the Parliament passed Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming 
Act, 2025 (“the Gaming Act”), which inter alia prohibited the offering of online money games. 
The Company has investment in one of its associate, Moonshine Technology Private 
Limited(‘the associate company’) and subsidiary, Halaplay Technologies Private Limited 
(‘the subsidiary company) aggregating to ` 1,05,855 Lakhs and ` 41 Lakhs before the 
enactment of the Gaming Act. The sole business of the associate company and subsidiary 
company was to offer online money games. The notification of the Gaming Act had lead 
to complete cessation of it’s entire operations including revenue-generating activities 
through online real money games. Consequently, the management of the Company 
has assessed the recoverable amount of these investments in accordance with the 
provisions of Ind AS 28 – Investments in associates and joint ventures read with Ind AS 
36 – Impairment of Assets. Accordingly, the Company has recognised an impairment loss 
amounting to ` 98,894 Lakhs w.r.t. an associate and ` 41 Lakhs w.r.t. one of the subsidiary 
during the year ended March 31, 2026, which is disclosed as an exceptional item.
	
The corresponding deferred tax asset has not been recognised on such impairment loss 
as it is not probable that the sufficient taxable profits will be available against which such 
asset can be realised.
H	
On November 13, 2025, the Company acquired 2,791 equity shares of ` 100 each, 
representing 8.37% of the equity share capital of Next Wave Multimedia Private Limited 
(“”NextWave””), for a total consideration of ` 500 Lakhs. Pursuant to this acquisition, the 
Company’s shareholding in NextWave increased from 74.88% to 83.25%.
	
Subsequently, on December 30, 2025, the Company acquired an additional 1,396 equity 
shares of ` 100 each, representing 4.19% of the equity share capital of NextWave, from 
the Sellers for a consideration of ` 250 Lakhs. Following this acquisition, the Company’s 
shareholding in NextWave increased from 83.25% to 87.44%.
	
Further, on March 31, 2026, the Company acquired 4,188 equity shares of ` 100 each, 
representing 12.56% of the equity share capital of NextWave, from the Sellers for an 
aggregate consideration of ` 750 Lakhs. Consequent to this acquisition, the Company’s 
shareholding in NextWave increased from 87.44% to 100%, thereby making NextWave a 
wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.”

basis by way of private placement to Axana Estates LLP (“the Allottee”) for an aggregate
